summaries.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is the open, Apache 2.0 tool protocol that Anthropic created and donated on 2025-12-09 to the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation. It is the cross-vendor way agents reach tools on AWS AgentCore, Microsoft Copilot, Google, OCI, OpenAI and Snowflake. The current spec, 2026-07-28, is stateless and deprecates HTTP+SSE in favor of Streamable HTTP. Its optional authorization uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, RFC 9728 metadata and Client ID Metadata Documents.

Model Garden is Google Cloud's model catalog, renamed from Vertex AI Model Garden on 2026-04-22. It lists Gemini, Veo and Lyria, partner models such as Anthropic Claude, Grok and Mistral, and open models such as Llama, Gemma and Qwen. Partner models like Claude are billed through Google Cloud. Before anyone can call one, an admin with the Consumer Procurement Entitlement Manager role must click Enable on the model's card, and the Consumer Procurement API must be allowed.

MuleSoft Agent Fabric is Salesforce MuleSoft's generally available layer for governing and connecting agents. Its parts are Agent Registry, Agent Broker for multi-agent orchestration, Agent Visualizer, Scanners, MCP Bridge, and Agent Governance, which covers a unified LLM and MCP Gateway, evals, trusted agent identity, a kill switch and cost controls. It makes agents A2A-compliant through pre-built connectors, and its registry lists public MCP servers. The status of Topic Center is unconfirmed.

NetSuite is Oracle's cloud ERP, and it connects to Oracle Cloud EPM. New customers integrate through the NetSuite EPM Connector SuiteApp, while the Sync SuiteApps add metadata loads, write-back, saved searches and EPM jobs. Existing NSPB Sync customers keep NSPB Sync. OAuth 2.0 support for NetSuite connections arrived in EPM 26.10 and 26.11, and the Connections REST APIs manage these connections.

OAuth 2.0 is the industry-standard delegated authorization framework, and almost every agent platform uses it for tool and API access. AgentCore supports M2M and user-federation flows. Copilot Studio, Agentforce, OpenAI and Snowflake use it to authenticate MCP servers, and Snowflake Cortex Agents MCP connectors accept OAuth only. Oracle recommends it over Basic Authentication for Cloud EPM REST and EPM Automate. OpenAI does not store the MCP token, so it must be resent on every request.

summaries.key: oauth 2 0 resource owner password credentials flow
summaries.summary: The Resource Owner Password Credentials (ROPC) flow is an OAuth 2.0 flow in which the app sends a user's username and password directly. In Microsoft Azure Identity it appears as UsernamePasswordCredential, or as DefaultAzureCredential with the AZURE_USERNAME and AZURE_PASSWORD variables. It cannot work with MFA, so it breaks under Entra mandatory multifactor authentication. It is deprecated in MSAL and the Azure Identity libraries, and automation should move to workload identities.

The OCI Agent Development Kit (ADK) is Oracle's client-side library for building agents on OCI Generative AI Agents, released 2025-05-22. For Python it ships as oci.addons.adk, installed with pip install "oci[adk]" and needing Python 3.10 or later. For Java it ships as bmc-addons/bmc-adk. It can attach MCP servers through the MCPClientStreamableHttp and MCPClientStdio toolkits.

OCI Audit is Oracle Cloud Infrastructure's service that records API calls. It identifies the calling principal, for example the instance OCID for instance principals. Logs are kept for 365 days, a tenancy-wide setting, so export them to Object Storage to keep them longer. No list of Generative AI or Agents audit event types was found.

The OCI CLI is Oracle's command-line tool for OCI, currently version 3.96.2 (2026-11-10). It installs through pip, MSI, a PowerShell script, or winget per third-party catalogs. It authenticates with API keys from oci setup config, browser session tokens, or instance and resource principals, chosen with --auth or OCI_CLI_AUTH. Agent work uses the generative-ai, generative-ai-agent, db, fn and related command groups. oci raw-request signs any REST call.

The OCI Database Tools MCP Server is Oracle's managed MCP server for Oracle AI Databases in OCI, introduced 2026-05-12. It reaches Autonomous, Base and Exadata databases through Database Tools connections, reportedly at no extra charge. It offers built-in tools such as run-sql plus custom SQL and PL/SQL tools. Auth is OAuth 2.0 through IAM identity domains, invocation needs use database-tools-mcp-servers-invocation, and it runs NL2SQL output as the end user. GA status is unconfirmed.

An OCI dynamic group is an Oracle IAM group whose members are resources matched by rules rather than users. This is how instances, Functions, Generative AI agents, ingestion jobs and hosted deployments are granted access through policies. Matching rules use resource.type values such as genaiagent, fnfunc or generativeaihosteddeployment, but free-form tags are not supported for Functions. Agent runtimes need dynamic groups or resource-principal policies, so request them on day one of an engagement.

OCI Functions is Oracle's serverless runtime, based on the Fn Project, and is commonly used to host agent tools. Functions authenticate as resource principals through dynamic groups, and tokens are cached for 15 minutes, so policy changes can lag by that long. Sync calls default to 30 seconds (maximum 300). Detached calls, which are GA, run up to 3,600 seconds. Payloads are capped at 6 MB. Use oci fn function invoke in production and fn invoke for development.

OCI Generative AI is Oracle's managed AI service, now positioned as the Enterprise AI Platform. It hosts Cohere, Gemini, Llama, gpt-oss and Grok models along with imported models, guardrails, the Responses API, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, projects and hosted agents. Access uses compartment-scoped IAM policies on generative-ai-family or narrower types, or API keys for testing. IAM signing is recommended for production. It does not retain prompts, and Gemini and Grok requests leave OCI.

OCI Generative AI Agents is Oracle's older standalone managed-agent service, GA since 2024. It offers RAG, SQL and agent-as-a-tool tools, custom function and API tools, and endpoints with sessions. It still has its own docs and its own genai-agent-family IAM family, with no deprecation announced, and it sits beside the newer Enterprise AI Agents. Agents act as resource principals that need policies to call models and read secrets. Default limits are 2 agents and 3 knowledge bases.

summaries.key: oci generative ai agents rag tool
summaries.summary: The RAG tool is a ready-to-use retrieval tool in Oracle's OCI Generative AI Agents. It supports hybrid lexical plus semantic search. Its knowledge base can be service-managed OCI Object Storage, with text and PDF files. It can also be bring-your-own vector search in Oracle AI Database 26ai, MySQL HeatWave, or OCI Search with OpenSearch.

OCI Generative AI API keys are bearer secrets created in the Generative AI service, not IAM signing keys, and have been available since 2026-01-21. They work only for the OpenAI-compatible endpoints in the same region and are not accepted by NL2SQL. Each key has two secrets that are shown once and expire after three months by default, with a limit of 100 keys per tenancy. A policy matching request.principal.type='generativeaiapikey' must grant access, and Oracle recommends them only for testing.

summaries.key: oci generative ai dedicated ai cluster
summaries.summary: A dedicated AI cluster is an OCI Generative AI serving mode that hosts a model on reserved hardware, not shared with other customers, behind an endpoint you create. Imported models require one. The tenancy limit defaults to 0, so file a limit increase before creating one. Each hosting cluster allows up to 50 endpoints. Billing is per unit-hour, with a 744-unit-hour minimum for hosting that imported models are exempt from.

summaries.key: oci generative ai enterprise ai agents
summaries.summary: OCI Enterprise AI Agents is the agent layer inside Oracle's OCI Generative AI and went GA on 2026-03-31. It added the OCI Responses API, projects, hosted applications, vector stores, NL2SQL and API keys. Agents are built with the API-first Responses API and OCI-managed tools, with hosted agentic applications, or with both. It sits beside the older Generative AI Agents service rather than replacing it, and it launched in nine regions including Chicago, Ashburn and Frankfurt.

GenerateText was Oracle's original OCI Generative AI text-generation API. It was deprecated in 2025, and the Generative AI release notes give 2025-06-26, while a deprecation notice says 2025-05-29. It, along with SummarizeText, became unavailable on 2026-06-26. Agent builders should use the Chat and Responses APIs instead.

OCI Generative AI Guardrails is Oracle's safety layer for models, GA for on-demand models since 2026-02-09 and for dedicated endpoints since 2026-02-26. It covers content and image moderation, prompt injection detection, PII detection and topic management, and the PII and topic features are English only. On-demand models apply it through the ApplyGuardrails API, while dedicated endpoints use Inform or Block mode. Versions can be pinned with guardrailVersionConfig.

Hosted applications are Oracle OCI Generative AI's way to deploy agentic applications, which run as resource principals. There are four inbound auth modes. Identity domain bearer tokens use the client credentials grant. Browser sessions use OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, GA since 2026-10-07. OCI IAM request signatures have been accepted since 2026-07-15. A 'No authentication' mode, added 2026-10-21, requires the app to enforce its own access control.

Model import is the OCI Generative AI feature, GA since 2025-11-12, that brings your own models from Hugging Face or OCI Object Storage into Oracle's service. Imported models must run on a dedicated AI cluster but are exempt from its 744-hour minimum. They have worked with the OCI Responses API since 2026-09-06. Recent imports include DeepSeek V4, Qwen 3.x, Nemotron 3, GLM-5.3, Kimi K3 and Gemma 4.

NL2SQL is an Oracle OCI Generative AI Enterprise AI feature that turns natural language into SQL but does not run it. It uses a semantic store with two Database Tools connections: a higher-privilege one for enrichment and a lower-privilege one for queries. The SQL is run through the Database Tools MCP Server as the end user. Its endpoints accept only IAM-signed requests, never API keys. The default model is openai.gpt-oss-120b, and model selection and scheduled enrichment were added in August 2026.

The OpenAI-compatible API lets the OpenAI SDK call Oracle's OCI Generative AI, which it has supported since 2025-11-05, at the regional base URL ending /openai/v1. It exposes responses, conversations, chat completions, files, vector stores and containers, but no embeddings path. Embeddings and rerank use the OCI-native API. Callers authenticate with API keys as bearer tokens or with IAM signing. An older path under 20231130/actions/v1 still exists.

An OCI Generative AI project is Oracle's container for responses, conversations, files, containers and sandboxes. The Responses API requires its OCID, which the OpenAI SDK sends as the OpenAI-Project header. A project can set short-term memory compaction and long-term memory, and neither can be disabled later without deleting the project. Retention is at most 720 hours. A tenancy allows 50 projects, and sandboxes are temporary Linux workspaces scoped to a project.

Identity domains are Oracle OCI IAM's identity layer and the successor to IDCS. They provide authentication, SSO, MFA and OAuth clients for OCI, Oracle SaaS such as Cloud EPM, and other apps. Each tenancy has a Default domain, and there are six domain types, from Free to Premium and External User. They support SAML 2.0 federation with IdPs such as Entra ID and Okta, plus OIDC and SCIM sync. They added Client ID Metadata Document support and OAuth resource indicators in fall 2026.

summaries.key: oci iam identity domain administrator role
summaries.summary: Identity Domain Administrator is the superuser role of an Oracle OCI IAM identity domain, and it is assigned separately from OCI IAM policies. It creates users, OAuth and confidential apps, Identity Propagation Trusts, SSO federation, sign-on policies, MFA and the Network Perimeter. For Cloud EPM it registers the public OAuth client with Device Code and Refresh Token grants and the AI Agent Studio confidential app. EPM user-management commands also require a Cloud EPM application role.

MFA in Oracle OCI IAM identity domains is configured by the Identity Domain Administrator or the Security Administrator, including for Cloud EPM. Users enroll an authenticator app, such as Oracle Mobile Authenticator or Google Authenticator, through 'Enable Secure Verification'. Users set up for Basic Authentication with MFA cannot call Cloud EPM REST APIs, so agent automation needs OAuth instead.

The Network Perimeter is an Oracle OCI IAM identity domain setting that allows or blocks IPs and CIDRs domain-wide, covering all EPM and EDM environments and Cloud Console sign-in. It replaced the per-environment IP allowlist commands and APIs, which were removed in EPM 26.05 (May 2026). The Identity Domain Administrator sets it up, and it must include an automation runner's egress IP and other regions' EPM outbound IPs. Whether it also restricts REST and EPM Automate calls is unconfirmed.

OCI IAM policies are Oracle Cloud's access statements, written as Allow <subject> to <verb> <resource-type> in <tenancy or compartment> with optional where conditions. Subjects are groups, dynamic groups, any-user or any-group, and the verbs build up from inspect to read, use and manage. Groups outside the Default domain must be qualified with their domain name. Cross-tenancy access needs paired endorse and admit statements. Tenancy administrators, or groups allowed to manage policies, write them.

Instance principals let Oracle OCI compute instances call OCI without stored credentials. OCI issues certificates and rotates them several times a day, and dynamic groups grant the access. Use them with --auth instance_principal or OCI_CLI_AUTH, the Python InstancePrincipalsSecurityTokenSigner, Terraform's auth = "InstancePrincipal", or OciInstancePrincipalAuth in oci-genai-auth. Every instance principal holds compartment_inspect, which cannot be revoked, and Audit logs the instance OCID as principalId.

Resource principals are Oracle OCI's credential-free identity for non-instance resources such as Functions, Generative AI agents, data ingestion jobs and hosted applications. They use a Resource Principal Session Token (RPST), a JWT with tenant and compartment claims. In Python use get_resource_principals_signer(), and in the CLI set OCI_CLI_AUTH=resource_principal. oci-genai-auth provides OciResourcePrincipalAuth. For Functions the token is cached for 15 minutes, so policy changes can lag.

The OCI Responses API is Oracle OCI Generative AI's OpenAI-style agent API, added with Enterprise AI Agents GA on 2026-03-31. It requires a project OCID. Its built-in tools are file_search, code_interpreter, function and remote mcp, the last over Streamable HTTP only with a raw token that is not stored. It added background mode and compaction in 2026. It is available in nine OC1 regions but not Dubai, and whether MCP Calling can reach private servers is unconfirmed.

OCI session tokens are Oracle's browser-based CLI credentials, created with oci session authenticate. They last 1 hour by default and can be refreshed with oci session refresh for up to 24 hours. Headless use relies on --no-browser or session export and import. Every command must pass --auth security_token or set OCI_CLI_AUTH, or it fails. They are unsupported in the PowerShell and Ruby SDKs, and oci-genai-auth provides OciSessionAuth.

OCI Signature Version 1 is Oracle Cloud's HTTP request-signing scheme for REST APIs. It is based on draft-cavage-http-signatures-08 with rsa-sha256, and the keyId is built from the tenancy OCID, user OCID and key fingerprint. POST and PUT must also sign the body hash, content type and length. Clock skew over 5 minutes, header or query mismatches, or a missing content-length cause a 401. NL2SQL endpoints accept only signed requests.

OCI Vault is Oracle Cloud's key and secrets service, and agents use it to store database and tool credentials. Its resource types include vaults, keys, key-delegate, secrets and secret-bundles, and secret-family groups the secret types. Reading secret content needs read secret-bundles. Generative AI agents read secrets through their resource principal with a genaiagent dynamic group. Customer-managed Vault keys can also encrypt fine-tuning data.

oci-genai-auth is Oracle's Python package that adds OCI IAM authentication to the OpenAI SDK for OCI Generative AI. Version 1.1.1 (2026-07-24) needs Python 3.9 or later. It provides httpx auth classes for session, user, instance and resource principals: OciSessionAuth, OciUserPrincipalAuth, OciInstancePrincipalAuth and OciResourcePrincipalAuth. They are used with api_key="not-used", the /openai/v1 base URL and a project OCID, and Oracle recommends this setup for production.

OKE Workload Identity lets pods on Oracle's OCI Kubernetes Engine call OCI as their Kubernetes service account. It works only on enhanced clusters, only through an OCI SDK, and cannot be used with dynamic groups. Policies use any-user with conditions on request.principal.type = 'workload', namespace, service account and cluster ID. It needs minimum SDK versions such as Python 2.111.0 and Go 65.32.0.

Okta is a third-party identity provider that agent platforms federate with for SSO and provisioning. It is a supported SAML 2.0 IdP for Oracle Cloud EPM, and it provisions users through SCIM into AWS IAM Identity Center and Snowflake. Databricks automatic identity management with Okta has been GA since 2026-07-03. Okta can also be a Snowflake External OAuth server and can issue ID-JAGs for OCI cross-app access.

Omnigent is Databricks' open-source (Apache 2.0) meta-harness for combining agents, and Databricks also offers a managed version. It coordinates Claude Code, Codex and custom agents defined in YAML, and Agent Bricks recommends it for multi-agent coordination. The launch blog calls the open-source project alpha, while the managed version is described as Beta. All of this comes from secondary sources.

OpenAI is the AI vendor behind the API platform, ChatGPT and Codex. Its flagship API models are the GPT-6 family, and its official SDKs read OPENAI_API_KEY. Access passes six control boundaries, and projects, keys and users are managed through the Admin API, since no Terraform provider was found. It holds SOC 2, ISO 27001 and 42001 and FedRAMP 20x, and supports HIPAA through a BAA. MCP is its tool protocol, and no A2A support was found.

The OpenAI Admin API automates organization management: invitations, users, groups, roles, projects, service accounts, API keys, spend limits, data retention, rate limits, audit logs, and usage and cost. It requires an Admin API key, set as OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY, and minimum SDK versions such as Python 2.34.0 and Node 6.36.0. Project service accounts are created under /organization/projects/{project_id}/service_accounts.

An OpenAI Admin API key is a credential for organization administration endpoints only, and it cannot call model or other non-admin endpoints. Only org owners can manage these keys. Set it as OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY when using the Admin API, with minimum SDK versions such as Python 2.34.0 and Node 6.36.0.

Agent Builder is OpenAI's visual workflow builder, part of AgentKit, which launched at DevDay on 2025-10-06. Its deprecation was announced 2026-06-03, and it shuts down on 2026-11-30. To migrate, export the workflow code to the Agents SDK with the Code button, or move to ChatGPT Workspace Agents.

The OpenAI Agents API is OpenAI's managed Codex-style agent harness at /v1/agents. It has been in public beta since 2026-09-10 and requires the OpenAI-Beta: agents=v1 header. It supports compaction, multi-agent, MCP tools, computer use and scheduled automations, in OpenAI-hosted, self-hosted or no environments. Keys need the api.agents.read, api.agents.write and api.responses.write scopes. It is US-only for data residency and has no Zero Data Retention.

The OpenAI Agents SDK for Python is OpenAI's open-source agent framework, the package openai-agents at version 0.24.0, which needs Python 3.10 or later. It uses the Responses API by default. It provides agents, handoffs, guardrails, sessions, tracing, sandbox agents, MCP tools, realtime agents and voice pipelines. It is the main migration target for Agent Builder workflows.

The OpenAI Agents SDK for TypeScript is OpenAI's JavaScript agent framework, the npm package @openai/agents at version 0.22.0. It builds on the core, openai and realtime subpackages. It provides MCPServerStdio, MCPServerSSE and MCPServerStreamableHttp for MCP, and @openai/agents/realtime for voice over WebRTC or WebSocket. Like the Python SDK, it includes SandboxAgent.

OpenAI API data residency keeps data storage, and in some regions processing, in a chosen region through regional domain prefixes such as eu.api.openai.com. The region is fixed when a project is created and cannot be changed. A Global project can instead enable per-request residency. Responses and Chat Completions are processed regionally in the US, EU, UAE, Australia, India and Japan. Regional endpoints cost 10% more for models released on or after 2026-03-05.

OpenAI's deprecations page tracks model and endpoint shutdowns that agents must migrate away from. Many legacy models are already gone, including gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4, gpt-4o-2024-05-13, o1, o3-mini, o4-mini (2026-10-23), computer-use-preview, and the gpt-5.x codex and chat-latest models. Upcoming shutdowns are tts-1 and gpt-realtime in January 2027, gpt-image-2 and whisper-1 in February 2027, and gpt-5.1 and gpt-5.4-nano on 2027-04-01.
